name: Non-AES power S-boxes: fewer AND gates at AND depth two
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for affine-basis search and small SAT resynthesis; exact checks evaluate only 32 or 128 inputs
statement: Marie Bolzer, Sébastien Duval and Marine Minier, A Tool for Lightweight (AND, XOR) Implementations of Large-Degree S-boxes, TCHES 2026(2), 605–629, ask about optimal (AND depth, AND count) in section 7.4. Tables 4 and 6 give depth-two implementations: in GF(32), x^30 uses 12 ANDs and x^21 and x^25 use 10 each; in GF(128), x^7 uses 30 and x^11 uses 27. The polynomial bases use z^5+z^2+1 and z^7+z+1. The XOR counts are respectively 51,37,37,140,115. Here x^30 is inversion with zero mapped to zero; x^21 and x^25 invert x^3 and x^5 as permutations. These five exact functions are outside the upstream AES and binary-multiplier targets.
success_criterion: Give a complete acyclic circuit for any one of these five exact vectorial functions, with AND depth at most 2 and respectively at most 11, 9, 9, 29 or 26 binary AND gates. Binary XOR and NOT, constants and fan-out are allowed; list and count every gate. NOT and XOR have zero multiplicative depth. No bound is imposed on XOR count, but all affine input/output conversions must appear in the circuit. Outputs must equal the specified field power in the specified basis, for every input. Also strictly improve the best comparable published result at claim time, including compatible compositions of published objects. State whether the candidate is a composition and identify its components. Values in unmerged pull requests do not set the bar.
verification_method: Independently implement polynomial-basis field arithmetic by carryless multiplication and reduction. Evaluate the candidate on every 5- or 7-bit input and compare all output bits with repeated-squaring exponentiation. Check the DAG, gate types, AND count and maximum number of AND nodes on any input-output path. Recompute algebraic degree by a Boolean Möbius transform as a consistency check. The truth tables and integer gate counts need seconds, not probabilistic testing.
status_checked: 2026-10-15 (supplied literature-status date; primary publication re-read 2026-10-24, later literature not independently rechecked)
angles: Reproduce the published basis transformations, then resynthesize small nonlinear cuts with an AND-count objective.
Search affine-equivalent representatives and account for the linear maps on both sides.
Try shared quadratic intermediates between output coordinates, with an explicit two-AND-layer constraint.
pitfalls: AND depth must stay at most two.
AND count, total gate count, masked cost and gate equivalents are different metrics.
The inverse-Gold exponents modulo 31 are 21 and 25; inversion is exponent 30.
Include all affine basis conversions in the circuit.
The paper confirms these implementations; later literature and composed circuits need a fresh comparison.
